what_was_wrong: R199 treated tokens_chunk_size as a free parameter and assumes token_overlap stays fixed at 2

real_code.real_num_chunks: pseudo_total = T - isolated + token_drop; pad to a multiple of tokens_chunk_size; num_chunks = pseudo_total//tcs - int(token_drop>0)

meaning: tokens_chunk_size is derived from clip_length, not tunable directly
token_overlap grows with chunk size, so bigger chunks waste MORE, not less
r199_error_magnitude: R199 claimed chunk=18 gives 0.816x; the real equivalent (clip_length=36) is 1.224x, i.e. 22 percent WORSE, so the recommendation pointed the opposite way

corrected_candidates.risk: moderate: chunk=4 overlap=1 keeps one blend window
corrected_candidates.memory: per chunk 20 frames versus 28 now, so memory goes DOWN and R199s memory worry is resolved
corrected_candidates.verdict: the only realistic candidate, just clears the target

corrected_candidates.risk: HIGH: overlap becomes 0, which means no boundary blend at all and therefore possible visible temporal seams; this is a quality change, far beyond a rounding difference, and not recommended

still_valid_from_r199: the observation that num_chunks=7 and 196 frames gives 1.58x overlap waste
the conclusion that the waste sits in decode_temporals chunking and that the pipeline side has no room
invalidated_from_r199: the claim that raising tokens_chunk_size saves 10-18 percent, which has the sign backwards
the memory-OOM worry, which does not apply to clip_length=16 because chunk frames drop
lesson: R199 treated a derived quantity as tunable without checking the assignment code, the same class of error as R189s missing head factor: compute first, verify after. The right order is to confirm in source what computes a quantity and whether it can change, then compute the payoff.
